---
title: "Installation"
---

`{baler}` ships as a native binary. There is no R package to install for the CLI itself, only for the `{box}` fork it depends on at runtime (see [below](#the-box-fork)).

## Pre-built binaries

Pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows are published on the [Releases](https://github.com/baler-dev/baler/releases) page.

1.  Linux / macOS:

    ``` bash
    curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baler-dev/baler/refs/heads/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
    ```

2.  Windows:

    ``` powershell
    powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baler-dev/baler/refs/heads/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex"
    ```

Both scripts download the archive for your platform from the latest release, and also the `.sha256` file published next to it. The archive is unpacked and installed only when its SHA-256 hash matches that file. On a mismatch, a missing checksum file or a malformed one, nothing is installed, and an existing `baler` stays as it was.

To pin a specific version, use that version's installer, which is published with every release and already knows its own tag:

``` bash
curl -LsSf https://github.com/baler-dev/baler/releases/download/v0.1.0/baler-installer.sh | bash
```

``` powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://github.com/baler-dev/baler/releases/download/v0.1.0/baler-installer.ps1 | iex"
```

On Linux and macOS, setting `BALER_VERSION` (for example `BALER_VERSION=v0.1.0`) pins the version when you run the script from `main`.

## Building from source

`{baler}` is a CLI tool built in Rust, so it requires the stable Rust toolchain (`rustc`, `cargo`). Once you managed to add the Rust toolchain, install `{baler}` from scratch via following command: 

``` bash
cargo install --git https://github.com/baler-dev/baler
```

The `baler` binary is built with the `network` feature of `baler-core` already on, so `--git` and `--url` installs work out of the box. The feature only matters if you use `baler-core` as a library: without it, those two install paths fail with an explicit "requires the 'network' feature" error rather than silently doing nothing.

### Verifying the install

``` bash
baler --version
```

## The `{box}` fork

`box-bale` modules are loaded through `{box}`, but the patches that make `box::use()` find `{baler}`'s install location aren't in upstream `{box}` yet. Until they land, use the [patched fork](https://github.com/joshuamarie/box/tree/feature/baler-support).

### Pre-built, no compiler needed

Releases ship the fork already built, for the current and the previous R version. If the build fails, the release goes out without these files, so if you don't see them, [build it yourself](#building-it-yourself). Pick the file for your platform:

| Platform | The file name ends with |
|---|---|
| Linux (Intel or AMD) | `_linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |
| Linux (ARM) | `_linux-aarch64.tar.gz` |
| macOS (Apple silicon) | `_macos-aarch64.tgz` |
| macOS (Intel) | `_macos-x86_64.tgz` |
| Windows | `_windows-x86_64.zip` |

The full name is `box_<version>_R<major.minor>_<platform>`, for example `box_1.2.3.261119_R4.5_linux-x86_64.tar.gz`. It has to match your R version, so check your R version by running `R.version$version.string` in R or run `R --version` and look at the first two numbers (4.5.2 means `R4.5`).

1.  Download the file and its `.sha256` from the [releases page](https://github.com/baler-dev/baler/releases).

2.  Check the download. On Linux run `sha256sum -c <file>.sha256`, on macOS `shasum -a 256 -c <file>.sha256`, and on Windows compare the output of `Get-FileHash <file>` with the `.sha256` file.

3.  Rename it to `box_<version>.<extension>`, such as `box_1.2.3.261119.tar.gz`. R reads the package name and version from the file name, and a longer name makes the install fail on some platforms.

4.  Install it:

    ``` bash
    R CMD INSTALL box_1.2.3.261119.tar.gz
    ```

The files on the latest release are rebuilt when the fork changes (it is checked every 6 hours), so they follow it. Older releases keep the files they shipped with, and a release that shipped without them stays that way.

### Building it yourself

If there is no file for your platform or R version, for example right after a new R release, compile the fork instead. 

``` r
# install.packages('pak')
# This needs compilation
pak::pak("joshuamarie/box@feature/baler-support")
```
